findings.summary: The overview chart's plot is about 415px tall at 1440, well past the 240px `size.chart` cap. The agent grew the plot so the chart panel ends level with Recent activity, because the tests fix the activity list at 5 items and it cannot be trimmed (dashboard agent-report.md, 'Chart height'). The spec offers only two ways to level side-by-side panels: grow the shorter up to the cap, or trim the longer. When neither works, it gives no third option, so the spec's wording contributes. rc.8 solved the same case with a totals row under the plot (Total / Peak / Average) and kept the plot near 240px. Published 1.1.0 also had a tall plot (about 340px, in full-strength cyan). The rc.9 bars are mixed down to muted teal, so they do not outweigh the 48px KPIs. The KPIs still read first. That makes this a weaker detail rather than a hierarchy break, and not worse than published. A general rule would close it: when the longer panel cannot be trimmed, fill the shorter one with a summary row or caption, never past `size.chart`.

The tote is back to one squared hollow arch over a box. Step 5's name test lists this outline as a usual cause of misreading. At 1x in the grid it reads as a generic shopping-bag icon or a padlock, and at detail size it reads as a padlock more than a canvas tote. It is still better than published 1.1.0, which had a narrow shackle over a small box: the handle now spans about 43% of the width, and the body is wide with a pocket. But it loses rc.8's two separate handle loops. The duffel (two square loops on a low box) and the tote still differ in outline, so set-mates are told apart.

In the blog hero, the left half of the near ground is outlined by a continuous 1-unit teal line that drops into square notches at regular intervals. It reads as a pipe, a circuit trace or a battlement rather than terrain. The reference's hill edge is an irregular lit grass line with tufts, not a geometric outline (reference p1-i1.png). The rise under the lead and the diagonal path are fine.

notes: SCOPE (screen step, 1 sample). Run folders: showcase/runs/night-cartridge/1.2.0-rc.9/<app>/20261018-112309/. Published = 1.1.0-rc.2/<app>/20261015-034853/. Earlier verdict = 1.2.0-rc.8/critic-1.json. Every gate passes in all four apps (eval-1.md). Palette consistency is 0.938 and type consistency is 1. The harness measured no layout defects, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. Not penalized (known harness gaps): the sticky header captured mid-page in full-page state shots (commerce state-checkout-errors, dashboard state-empty-filter, blog state-newsletter-error) and the dialog scrim ending at about 900px (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png).

RC.8 MAJORS. (1) Garment sleeves: FIXED. The sweater is one silhouette, and its sleeves flare out from the shoulders with the cuffs farther out than the joint, fill against fill (commerce drawings/home-d6.png, products-merino-crew-sweater-desktop-light.png). The coat's sleeves are attached and splay to cuffs (drawings/home-d4.png). Sweater, coat and tee now differ in outline: the coat is long with a collar, the tee is short-sleeved and boxy (drawings/home-d8.png). No straight bars hang beside a body anywhere in the grid. (2) Item-card summaries clamped at 2 lines: FIXED. Every product summary is whole in up to 3 lines at 1440 ('Water-resistant backpack for commutes and short hikes.', 'A two-night bag with a separate shoe compartment.', 'A lightweight knit for layering in every season.'; commerce home-desktop-light.png). Blog `.cards` show whole summaries of up to 4 lines (blog home-desktop-light.png).

UPDATE GOAL (1.2.0, leftovers from the 1.1.0 review): REACHED. Hero lead identity: a printing house with an 'INK' sign in real letters, a sawtooth roof with skylights, a chimney and a roller window (blog drawings/home-d1.png). Low confidence: at 1x the two round rollers can read as goggles. Mobile hero: the whole lead shows under a band of sky (blog home-mobile-light.png). Product-page sprite: about 49% of the window on desktop (products-merino-crew-sweater-desktop-light.png, tote 295 of about 606px) and about 45% on mobile (products-merino-crew-sweater-mobile-light.png). Sweater sleeves: reached (above). Newsletter title: an h2 ('Subscribe to the newsletter'). Store name on mobile: 'Fieldhouse Supply' in full. Hero hill: a rise under the lead with a teal rim and a diagonal stepped path to the bottom right. Mobile table: Project and Status only (dashboard home-mobile-light.png).

COMPARED WITH PUBLISHED 1.1.0: nothing worse. Better: the hero lead, sweater and coat, the tote (wider handle with a pocket, against published's narrow padlock shackle), the key ring (no longer a magnifier), detail banners with their own lead per item (TOTE and KNIT buildings with their own sign words, commerce drawings/products-*-d1.png), varied blog banner leads (TYPE house, NEWS kiosk, BOOK house, each about 105–117px tall), the mobile table and store name, and same-height controls. Equal: chart height (taller, but muted bars), the empty-state title size, the password form band, the user menu without a highlighted option and the crosses on the settings ridges. All four are carried rc.8 minors and are not re-raised.

SIGNATURE (4, up from 3). Present in all four apps and placed as Applying the concept says. Blog: a full-bleed hero, banners on articles and about, an inline figure (posts-shipping-a-design-system-d2.png), vignettes. Store: grid and cart strips, a banner per product. Dashboard and settings: a strip per screen with its own lead (OPS, HALL, KEYS, PAY). Every screen has the checkered ground strip. Motion is stepped: blog motion-m1.png shows nc-swap at 500ms with steps(1). The garment regression that held rc.8 at 3 is gone. Not a 5: strip props are still 20–50px and simpler than the reference's trees and figure at the same scale (dashboard drawings/home-d1.png vs reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png). The banners reuse one prop kit (water tower, lamp, board on legs, cat, crates), and there are the two minors above.

OTHER SCORES. Reference fidelity (4): night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dither rules under h2s, one gold commit with a hard shadow, the gold ▶ marker, hue top bars and square bullets, block meters and the grass strip, as in reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png, without copying the cabin, figure or snow. Cross-app consistency (4): one family. Blog and store use top navigation, dashboard and settings a sidebar, with the same windows, chips, meters and strip. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, 48px KPIs, a 48px price and a gold Add to cart. The empty-state title at body size is carried. Spacing (4): the 4px scale holds and panels end level; the chart cap is the minor above. Component states (4): card hover shows the marker and a lighter card (commerce state-card-hover-desktop-dark.png). Invalid fields get a gold focus frame on the first one, danger frames and '!' messages (commerce state-checkout-errors-desktop-dark.png, blog state-newsletter-error-desktop-dark.png). The plan change opens a titled window dialog with a framed close button, Cancel and a gold Confirm (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png). Loading shows skeleton KPI tiles and a disabled 'Refreshing ...' button (dashboard state-loading-desktop-dark.png). Empty results show a vignette, an empty 0-of-n meter and a framed ▶ Clear filters. Polish (4): radius 0, 2/4px borders, no leftover browser defaults.

AGENT REPORTS. The commerce agent says the key ring cannot have a 4×3 opening inside a ring at most 6 units across. That is not a real contradiction: a 6-wide ring of 1-unit runs leaves a 4-wide opening, and 6×5 outer gives 4×3. No spec change is needed; noted only because an agent read it as a conflict. The dashboard agent openly exceeded `size.chart` because the panel-levelling rule had no option left (minor finding 1).

VERDICT INPUT. No blocker and no major. Both rc.8 majors are fixed, the 1.2.0 update goal is reached, and nothing is worse than published 1.1.0. Three minors are listed once. The screen step passes; the candidate can go to the confirm step.
